metadata.topic: Organic Chemistry — Characteristics of a Homologous Series
metadata.note: Three characteristics of a homologous series: (1) same general formula, (2) members differ by CH₂, (3) gradual/similar change in physical/chemical properties. 3 slots × 1m each. Word bank: 5 tokens.

question.name: CSEC Chem Jan 2024 Q3b(i) — Characteristics of a Homologous Series
question.text:
List THREE characteristics of a homologous series by selecting the correct statements below.

Characteristic 1: [[1]]

Characteristic 2: [[2]]

Characteristic 3: [[3]]
question.general_feedback:
Characteristics of a homologous series:

  1. Same general formula — all members can be represented by one general formula (e.g. alkanes: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂)
  2. Members differ by CH₂ — consecutive members differ by one methylene (CH₂) group in their molecular formula
  3. Gradual change in physical properties — boiling point, melting point, and density increase gradually with increasing chain length

Also accepted: Similar chemical properties (same functional group), prepared by similar methods.

groups.label: Characteristic 1 of a homologous series
groups.diagnostic_hint: One key characteristic is that all members share the same general formula (e.g., CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ for alkanes). This means their molecular formulae follow a pattern.

groups.label: Characteristic 2 of a homologous series
groups.diagnostic_hint: A second characteristic: consecutive members differ by exactly one CH₂ unit (14 mass units). This regular increment is what makes it a "series".

groups.diagnostic_hint: Physical properties (boiling point, viscosity, density) change gradually and predictably as chain length increases — longer chains have stronger London dispersion forces.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 5 tokens for 3 slots; 3 correct + 2 distractors. 'All members have the same boiling point' — incorrect; boiling points INCREASE with chain length (same general formula ≠ same boiling point). Tests a common misconception. 'Members have the same molecular formula' — members of a homologous series have the SAME GENERAL formula but DIFFERENT molecular formulae. Engine awards 1m for any of the 3 correct tokens in each slot; de-duplication is a UX concern not modelled here.
